Since the weak convergence topology on $\mathcal{P}(X)$ requires a compatible topology on $X$, we may assume (as is standard) that $X$ is a separable metrizable space with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal{B}(X)$. **Step 2: Evaluation maps are Borel measurable.**

For each $A \in \mathcal{B}(X)$, the map $e_A: \mathcal{P}(X) \to [0,1]$, $p \mapsto p(A)$, is Borel measurable. Indeed, for closed $F \subseteq X$, we have $p(F) = \lim_{n \to \infty} \int f_n\,dp$ where $f_n(x) = \max(0,\, 1 - n\cdot d(x,F))$ are bounded continuous functions; each $p \mapsto \int f_n\,dp$ is continuous (hence Borel) by definition of the weak topology, so $p \mapsto p(F)$ is Borel. **Step 3: A countable generating algebra.**

Since $X$ is separable and metrizable, it has a countable base $\{U_n\}_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$. Let $\mathcal{A}$ be the algebra generated by $\{U_n\}$ (all finite unions of finite intersections of the $U_n$ and their complements). Then $\mathcal{A}$ is **countable** and $\sigma(\mathcal{A}) = \mathcal{B}(X)$.

We claim:
$$d(p,q) = \sup_{A \in \mathcal{A}} |p(A) - q(A)|.$$

$$\sup_{A \in \mathcal{A}} |p(A) - q(A)| \geq \sup_{B \in \mathcal{B}(X)} |p(B) - q(B)| = d(p,q).$$

This establishes the claim.

$$(p, q) \;\mapsto\; |p(A) - q(A)|$$
is Borel measurable on $\mathcal{P}(X) \times \mathcal{P}(X)$: it is the absolute value of $e_A \circ \pi_1 - e_A \circ \pi_2$, a difference of two measurable maps (compositions of the measurable evaluation map $e_A$ with the continuous projections $\pi_1, \pi_2$).

Since $\mathcal{A}$ is countable:
